A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Curvature Tuning and contain readable methods, experiments, equations, references, and appendices. Full-text inspection and rendered-page checks support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original transfer-learning, robustness, and ablation results for ResNets and Swin transformers, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V2 reports original CT and Trainable CT experiments, LoRA comparisons, robustness evaluations, synthetic classification results, and learned-parameter analyses.

M1.justification: The original shared-β activation with a fixed 0.5 mixing coefficient is retained. V2 additionally introduces Trainable CT, learning separate β and mixing coefficients c for output neurons/channels through backpropagation. V1's appendix code permits training a scalar β, but does not implement this jointly learned, channel-specific variant.

E1.justification: V2 removes the MNIST/CIFAR cross-pretraining and transfer study, CelebA multi-label prediction, dSprites orientation regression, and VOC2012 segmentation. It retains the twelve natural/medical classification datasets and CIFAR/ImageNet robustness evaluations, and adds the circular-boundary synthetic classification example in Figure 2. Thus task coverage changes substantially; CIFAR datasets are not removed entirely.

E2.justification: V1 compares CT principally against the original ReLU backbone; its LoRA table reports parameter counts without predictive-performance comparisons. V2 evaluates rank-1 LoRA against Trainable CT across ResNet and Swin transfer experiments and in the synthetic example, making an additional finetuning comparator central to the empirical evaluation.

E3.justification: V1 Section 3.3 explicitly selects β using test performance. V2 Section 4.1 selects β and checkpoints on validation data and reports corresponding test accuracy, with stratified 20% holdouts when validation splits are unavailable. Logistic-regression probing is replaced by 20-epoch Adam-trained classifiers, the reported β grid changes from [0.5,1) to [0.7,1], and new Trainable CT/LoRA training protocols are introduced. Robustness evaluation still selects the best benchmark β.

E4.justification: V1's Swish/SoftPlus component ablations, probing-regularization and feature-layer sensitivity tests, and CelebA attribute-specific versus global β analyses disappear. V2 adds the capacity/expressivity comparison in Figure 2 and learned β/c distribution analyses in Tables 6–7 and Figures 5–6. The β-search accuracy analysis is retained with revised datasets and validation curves.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three runs with seeds 42, 43, and 44. V1 provides per-result standard deviations throughout its appendix benchmark tables; v2 Tables 1–5 report means without corresponding benchmark-score deviations. V2 adds standard-deviation bands to validation and parameter-distribution plots. Its Tables 6–7 describe parameter dispersion across neurons and runs, rather than uncertainty in benchmark accuracy.

E6.justification: Transfer scores are extensively replaced under revised protocols, and Trainable CT/LoRA results are added, showing stronger average Trainable CT performance on ResNets but weaker performance than LoRA on Swin. The ResNet-50/CIFAR-10 ℓ∞ CT entry changes from 14.83% at β=0.95 to 12.08% at β=0.90. Most other robustness entries remain unchanged; larger headline percentages also reflect switching from pooled robustness improvements to attack-specific aggregation.

T1.justification: V2 adds Sobolev-space definitions, projection Theorems 3.1/C.1, derivative-bound Lemma C.2, proofs, and the circular-boundary approximation derivation in Appendix C. It also restricts the β→0 linear limit to c=1, correcting v1's assertion that both smoothing constructions become linear. The existing MASO theorem is retained under new numbering.

C1.justification: V1 centers a training-free steering contribution. V2 makes both steering and trainable finetuning core contributions, claims projection into smooth function spaces and increased local expressivity, and emphasizes complementary operation to weight adaptation and parameter efficiency relative to LoRA. Empirical headline claims shift toward twelve classification datasets and ℓ∞ robustness.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting larger optimal β to model capacity and U-shaped learned parameter distributions to activation flexibility. It explains Swin underperformance through limited pretraining and parameter capacity, and distinguishes substantial ℓ∞ gains from marginal corruption gains. Appendix C.1 explicitly leaves extending the projection result to Trainable CT for future work, adding an important applicability qualification.

D1.justification: V2 adds channel-aware Trainable CT replacement code, sigmoid-constrained parameterization, and LoRA linear/convolutional implementations. It documents validation-split construction, checkpoint selection, initialization, and separate learning rates for Trainable CT and LoRA. Hardware reporting adds an L40 GPU. The repository access link is retained, while implementation details tied to removed experiments disappear.

R1.justification: V1 concludes that CT and LoRA serve distinct needs; v2 substantially repositions CT as function-space adaptation complementary to feature/weight adaptation, supported by a new expressivity argument. It adds references to Hornik, Cybenko, RoAd, and Mamba, while removing several references associated with discarded tasks and implementations. The existing spline-theory reference is retained despite bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, explicitly distinguishing steering from finetuning. Method exposition and experimental sections are reorganized around CT, Trainable CT, and projection theory, and the appendices receive a new order and roadmap. Terminology changes from Swish to SiLU, and Matteo Gamba is added to the author list.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and tables are substantially redesigned and consolidated around method comparisons. Transfer β values move into a separate table. V2 adds the circular-boundary comparison and parameter-distribution figures, relocates v1 Figure 2 to Appendix A as Figure 3, and redraws/regroups the Swin learning curves. Numerous earlier appendix tables are removed.

improvement.justification: Validation-based transfer selection replaces v1's explicit test-set tuning, while actual LoRA comparisons and detailed implementation information make the empirical contribution more credible and assessable. These gains are partly offset by losing benchmark standard deviations and diagnostic ablations. Robustness still uses benchmark-selected β, and the new projection proof is restricted to finite samples and includes an unjustified positive-definite-Hessian assertion in Appendix C.1. These limitations constrain the overall quality gain.
